Chungking
Now. 3, 1938
Dear Bix:
I am waiting here at the office for Francis Pan who promised to come
by to see me about seven o'clock, and as I have over an hour I will start this
to you. I tried to go out to see Mr. Pan but he had to attend the Peoples Conference
which has been going on here for several days, so he said he would drop in here
after it was over.
Regarding this Peoples Conference I am all for it. It met in Hagkan
Hankow about three or four months ago and it brought forth some very constructive
criticisms on the Ministry of Railways and Communications. It had Dr. H. H. Kung
on the carpet the other day and grilled him for three hours. The point in dispute
was why he had placed his son David in charge of the Central Trust. I hear the
Bonference is composed of some of the ablest and most independent people in
China.
Another item of gossip around here is that China and the Soviets are not
getting along too well at the moment and that China may more or less cut loosa
from Russia. The Russians do not to seem to be getting much consideration from
anyone just now. Everyone seems to be climbing on the German band wagon.

munitions in which China agreed to pay for the transportation in Sterling or
us dollars but, refused to pay except in lex at the official rate. Unfortunately
the munitions were sold on credit which sort of cramped the Doctors style.

Socony has a boat there ready which can carry forty thousand gallons per trip but

the river is still too high for this small boat to get up the Gorges.
expect to start any day. Just now at Chungking we are borrowing gas from the
Aviation Commission five thousand gallons at the time and having to argue and
beg for it each time•
Regarding spare parts this is going to be less complicated for a while
because we do not have to worry about the Commodores and the Dolphis and the
They are only doing about one third of the flying they were doing and
if the Japanese take Ichang the Commodores will probably entirely so all we
shall have to consider are the DOtwos.
Unfortunately owing to the uncertainty
and the difficulty we were having in getting US dollars and the delay and the
large amount already in Hongkong for which CNAC owed PASCO, I cancelled all orders
already sent in and stop sending in any more. However now that we have cleared up
everything in Hong Kong I think it is safe to order what we need so we are
working on some orders that will cover our needs in this respect.
Regarding the adjustment of routes this is going to be a tough problem.
CNAC is flying Chungking Ichang three times per week and getting full loads out of
Ichang of evacuees but this will end soon and apparently the Japanese are pushing
on to Ichang with little resistance.
That leaves us with Chungkingwad Chengtu,
and Chungking Kunming both of which are booning and I think will bring us
nearly two hundred and fifty thousand dollars per month alone. We are also
trying to get into Hanoi from Chungking which I think will stand two wank trips
per week with probably seventy percent capacity. All of this will keep CNAC
in business very confortably and allow a small profit if we can continue to buy
US dollars at the official rate for our needs. We are also flying once a week to
Hongkong at night loaded to capacity but when we get into Hanoi we plan to cut
that out.
Eurasia is flying Hanoi Kunming twice a week with low percentage because
of the railway service competing. They also fly Kunming Chengtu and get very little
now that we are flying Chungking Kunming. They are also flying Chengtu Sian and
Sian Lanchow nuk but not getting much revenue. In September and October, after they lost
their Hongkong Hankow service I understand their losses were terrific and they are
all scared. They forget the big losses CNAC had when the war started and we loss all our
lines and had to develop others and how we were not allowed to share the Hankow
Hongkong line with Eurasia. Actually Eurasias lines are nearly as good as ours and
I am certain Eurasia could develop a profitable business with what they have if they
handled it properly but Eurasia as you know has its own system of dissipating its
profits and its reserve so that although it has had more revenue all this year
than CNAC and should have a big reserve it is just about on the rocks and the
Ministry is faced with the prospects of subsidizing them and the Ministry hasnt
the money. To try to talk justice or contract or logic to the Minister or the
Ministry would be like- well the most
useless thing you can think of, so I guess
there will be some sort of compromise but just now I am protesting like the .
deuce and threatening all sorts of things. I hope in the end to obtain, l) not too
great competition from Eurasia in schedules and the ability to reduce that through
superior operations and equipment, 2) the five year extension of our contract, IN
WRITING, 3) the the recognition as being permanent our newly developed lines
Chungking Hongkong and Chungking Kunming, 4) the Eurasia competition to cease when
the war is over. That is my idea of wishful thinking•
Anyway to get back to my original idea, if I can get these items settled

the first two pertaining to operations are not difficult, either we get gas or
we do not get gas and there is nothing we can do about it now, and the third item
pertaining to adjustment of schedules is going to be settled also whether I like
the settlement or not, ifxkxget these things work themselves out in time I still
have a faint hope of getting to the States for a month or two. My real reasons for
wanting to get home I gave above.
There is also the very urgent reason that I
very much need to get home and talk over all of the China problems with you and
Mr. Morgan. Sharp can handle the operations while I am away.
Actually I feel there is very little I can now accomplish that is of
concrete value except of course holding on and keeping the book velue of CNACás
high as possible as a basis for any future negotiations which may develop. I do not
think there is much chance of making any more collections for PAA. The old Route Three
debt is mostly liquidated, the Commodores are all paid for and you have a deposit of.
approximately US$20,000.00• Also CNAC will probably need all of its reserves now.
For these reasons if I can
arrange it, I do not think I would be neglecting my work
too much if arranged to make a trip to the States, provided nothing turns up to
compicate the situstion any more then it now is.
If you end Mr. Morgan have any
opinions on this I would be glad if you would write me. I hope you will approve
because I really think I need to get away from this show for a chanceto catch my breath.
Il this can be arranged I would like to fly home some where around the tenth
to the fifteenth of next month. Gosh just thinking about that gives me a shiver.
I guess this is about long enough. Francis Pan has just called to say he
was still in conference but would meet me at eight, but I told him it was so late
that it would be an imposition to ask him to come to my office to night so I would
see him in the morning at his office. Ihis Peoples Conference has all of them on
their toes and working over time.
Copy MR. MORGAN
Sincerely yours
Bonda
